chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, raising it, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Abu Basir, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), ‘May I be sacrificed for you; when will the relief be?’
So he said, ‘O Abu Basir, are you among those who desire the world? Whoever recognizes this matter has already been granted relief through awaiting it.’

key_terms.الدُّنْيَا: the worldly life and its immediate concerns
key_terms.الْفَرَجُ: the relief or deliverance being awaited
key_terms.لِانْتِظَارِهِ: through awaiting it, meaning patient expectancy of the affair
key_terms.هَذَا الْأَمْرَ: this matter, meaning the divinely ordained affair of the Imam

ai.seo_question: How does recognizing the Imam bring relief even before the faraj arrives?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true relief is not merely the outward occurrence of the awaited faraj, but begins with ma'rifah of the Imam and steadfast awaiting of the affair. It shifts attention from worldly impatience to spiritual certitude, presenting recognition of this matter as itself a form of deliverance.
